reason: E2 directly supports the mechanistic link between local chemical ordering, rugged energy landscapes, raised activation barriers, and altered dislocation behavior in a multi-principal-element alloy, but it concerns NiCoCr, not CoCrFeNiTi. E1 is about a different alloy (Al0.7CoCrFeNi) and different strengthening mechanisms (L12 precipitates), providing no support for the SRO-based premises. The extrapolation to CoCrFeNiTi and the claim that cooling rate alone can vary SRO without phase changes are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Short-range chemical order (SRO) can be varied in a single-phase solid-solution alloy by cooling rate alone
Increased SRO heightens the ruggedness of the energy landscape for dislocations
Increased SRO raises activation barriers for dislocation motion, enhancing strength/hardness
A more disordered state facilitates easier dislocation propagation, reducing strength and increasing ductility
These SRO-dislocation mechanisms apply to equimolar CoCrFeNiTi
